text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The caretaker government unfolded a 127 billion rupees 25-year National Drainage Programme for managing the country's irrigation system through cooperation between the government and private sector.
- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto criticised the latest amendments in the election laws and alleged these were aimed at protecting corrupt people and is an attempt to rig the elections.
- An earth quake of mild intensity shook Karachi in the early hours of Friday.

- The police will produce Asif Ali Zardari, husband of Benazir Bhutto, and two government officers accused for involvement in the alleged murder of Murtaza Bhutto, before a magistrate on Saturday for keeping them in their custody for further interrogations.
- A toy bomb killed two boys and wounded another boy near the city of Peshawar.
- The caretaker defence minister Shahid Hamid has been given the additional portfolio of law and parliamentary affairs after the resignation of Fakhruddin G.Ebrahim.
- Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves which excludes gold reserves may fall below $600 million by end of December 1996.
- The net outflow of portfolio investment during the first five months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) was $8.15 million compared to a net inflow of $27 million in the same period last year.

- The Pakistani rupee is likely to weaken further in 1997 after losing over 17 percent of its dollar value this year because of high inflation, a huge trade deficit and low foreign exchange reserves, analysts said.
- Liquid forex reserves registered an increase for the second consecutive week to $790 million from $745 million, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said.
